subject: closing the hole I found and left open last turn

the_vulnerability_confirmed.method: corrupted a claim on a scratch copy, then appended "|| true" to the verify script
the_vulnerability_confirmed.meaning: two words in package.json make a corrupted repo report healthy

built: scripts/audit-verify-chain.mjs — inspects the chain DEFINITION rather than the artifacts
catches: a gate named in the chain but absent from disk
a gate on disk but dropped from the chain
all_four_verified: each defect injected on a scratch copy produced exactly one finding of the right kind

my_fix_did_not_work_the_first_time.what_i_did: put the guard FIRST in the verify chain
my_fix_did_not_work_the_first_time.why: "|| true" wraps the WHOLE chain including the guard — it exits 4 standalone and 0 through npm
my_fix_did_not_work_the_first_time.the_principle: a guard cannot protect the mechanism that invokes it
my_fix_did_not_work_the_first_time.how_i_caught_it: ran the end-to-end test instead of trusting that the gate fired in isolation

the_actual_fix.what: a pre-push hook that calls the guard DIRECTLY, outside the chain, before running the chain
the_actual_fix.caveat: .git/hooks/ is not version-controlled, so this protects THIS clone only. The script is committed as .githooks-pre-push with npm run hooks:install. A fresh clone is unprotected until someone runs it — stated rather than glossed.

a_claim_this_confirms: GQ-001 says the gates "have blocked ZERO pushes: verify runs by habit and stops voluntarily, so it is a pre-commit convention rather than an enforcement boundary." There were no git hooks at all until now. The claim was exactly right, and this is the first thing in the repo that can actually stop a push.
